channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Two cargo vessels were seized in the Gulf of Aden within four days, bringing to at least 13 the number of ships attacked off Somalia this year and prompting drone strikes against the pirates — the largest escalation in hijackings in more than ten years.
item.description:
The resurgence adds a second source of maritime risk to shipping already constrained by the blockade and conflict arising from the US war with Iran. At least 13 vessels have been attacked since the start of the year, with two seizures in the Gulf of Aden inside four days, and the response has included drone strikes against the pirates, described as unprecedented. The region is a critical corridor for international trade, and the escalation has renewed concern about security there. The wider maritime toll of the conflict is now measurable: the International Maritime Organization has verified at least 70 attacks on international shipping in the Persian Gulf since the war began on 28 February. Separately, it reports that 19 seafarers have been killed in attacks on international shipping and at least 6,000 remain aboard hundreds of ships unable to leave.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Risk on the Gulf of Aden approaches matters because it sits on the Red Sea corridor toward Suez, a route many carriers are already avoiding in favour of the longer passage around southern Africa. A second security problem on that path could affect war-risk insurance premiums, routing decisions and transit times for raw materials and finished goods moving between Asia and Europe, independently of how the Hormuz position develops. Points that may be worth considering include whether freight assumptions distinguish between the Hormuz disruption and this separate risk on the Red Sea approaches, since the two could ease or worsen on different timelines.

BBC News | The New Indian Express

item.title: Low water on the Danube forced Romania's Nuclearelectrica to disconnect a reactor on 13 August and Hungary to shut one in early August, and France's agriculture ministry reported yield losses above 50% for some crops, with 65% of the country in drought.
item.description:
The Danube's level left insufficient cooling water for reactors in Eastern Europe: Romania's state operator Nuclearelectrica disconnected the only running reactor at Cernavodă on 13 August, and Hungary shut a reactor in early August for the same reason. A separate three-reactor shutdown at France's Gravelines plant had a different cause — an influx of jellyfish clogging the cooling intake — and is not a drought effect. In France, the agriculture ministry said yield losses have exceeded 50% for some crops, with drought affecting 65% of the territory; market gardening was the worst hit, cited in 81 departments, followed by maize, arboriculture, open-field vegetables and viticulture. Harvests are expected to be historically low, and the government will detail an aid plan on 3 September running to several hundred million euros, aimed largely at farms that carry no insurance — only about 68,000 of France's 400,000 farms are insured. France Assureurs separately put insured damage from the wildfires in Gironde, Landes and Var since 21 July at close to EUR 500 million across some 25,000 claims, on an initial assessment using data through mid-August. On the Rhine, experts warn that recurring low water is creating costly challenges for the companies that depend on the river to move raw materials, chemicals and energy products, and that such disruptions could become more common in the years ahead.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Two channels reach chemical and adhesive technologies production directly. The two Danube reactor outages are individually small, but they show cooling-water availability becoming a constraint on generation at a time when energy costs are already elevated, and low water on the Rhine constrains the barge movements that carry feedstocks and finished product through the German industrial corridor. The agricultural losses feed through more slowly, to bio-based feedstock availability and to food and beverage customers whose demand drives packaging adhesives. Points that may be worth considering include whether European logistics and energy planning still treats low-water periods as exceptional rather than recurring.

Commercial Times | Les Echos | MarketScreener | Challenges | Deutsche Welle

item.title: China's official manufacturing PMI rose 0.6 points to 49.8 in August and the non-manufacturing index was unchanged at 49.0, leaving both below the 50 mark separating expansion from contraction, with equipment and high-tech manufacturing the exceptions.
item.description:
The National Bureau of Statistics and the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing reported the manufacturing purchasing managers' index at 49.8, up 0.6 points from July but still in contraction; the composite output index rose 0.2 points to 49.5. The detail shows a two-speed picture. Production and new-order indices for electrical machinery and equipment and for computer, communication and other electronic equipment were all above 53, and the equipment-manufacturing and high-tech manufacturing PMIs stood at 51.4 and 52.9. Company size mattered too: large enterprises moved above the line to 50.6, medium-sized firms slipped to 49.4, and small firms improved 0.5 points but stayed well below at 47.9. In the non-manufacturing survey, civil-engineering construction activity rose almost two points to above 52, and the construction industry index eased slightly to 46.9. The business-activity expectation index fell 0.4 points to 55.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

For suppliers into China, the aggregate number understates the divergence underneath it. Demand tied to electronics, equipment and high-tech manufacturing is expanding, which is where higher-specification adhesive technologies tend to be used, and infrastructure-linked civil engineering is picking up. Building construction and smaller manufacturers remain the weaker parts, which may affect volume-driven construction-chemicals demand and the payment behaviour of smaller customers. Points that may be worth considering include whether the current China product and customer mix is weighted toward the segments that are growing or the ones still contracting.

Commercial Times | China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing | Commercial Times | China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing

item.title: Germany's CDU/CSU and SPD groups adopted a paper calling for stronger protection of German and European industry from imports, which group sources said refers mainly to Chinese overcapacity. Chinese brands passed 11% of Europe's car market in July.
item.description:
The paper was agreed at a closed meeting of the governing parliamentary groups' executive committees in Münster. It backs the European Commission and the German government in advancing further EU trade and investment agreements, and calls for stronger protection of German and European industry. China is not named in the text, but sources from the parliamentary groups said the concern is primarily Chinese overcapacity. Business bodies are engaged but measured: the German Chambers of Commerce and Industry's head of foreign trade, Volker Treier, said Germany needs to discuss the trade situation with China, and that if the problems are confirmed to stem from subsidies or unfair competition then that is a problem — adding that existing WTO and EU instruments are sufficient to protect European industry. The market data underline the pressure: Dataforce reported that Chinese brands took more than 11% of Europe's overall car market in July, and about a third of registered plug-in hybrids, with BYD and models such as Chery's Jaecoo drawing buyers on price.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The automotive supply chain is one of the largest markets for industrial adhesives, coatings and sealants, so a shift in where vehicles sold in Europe are built has a direct bearing on where that demand sits and who the customers are. A governing-coalition position in Germany moves trade defence from a Commission-level debate toward a national political commitment, which may raise the likelihood of measures being adopted. Points that may be worth considering include the commercial balance between established European carmakers and the Chinese manufacturers gaining share, and whether supplier relationships reflect that shift. The paper sets a direction rather than a measure.

Handelsblatt | Lianhe Zaobao | Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will encourage G20 members to re-examine their terms of trade with China and consider further barriers, calling the flood of Chinese exports unsustainable, as finance leaders met in Asheville from 31 August.
item.description:
Speaking before the meeting, Bessent argued that G20 countries should look again at their trading relationships with China as part of reducing global imbalances and pressing Beijing to rebalance its economy from exports toward domestic consumption, adding that the US direct trade position with China was "rapidly improving". The agenda he set out also covers severing business ties with Iran, boosting growth, and addressing concerns about US debt and rising bond yields. US officials said they would stress the importance of complying with the Iran sanctions. The meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors in Asheville, North Carolina, is the first of several ministerial meetings before a G20 leaders' summit that Trump will host in Florida in December. It convenes against an unsettled backdrop of uncertainty over the administration's next tariff moves, the dispute with Canada, and high energy and commodity prices linked to the Iran war.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

An explicit US push for other G20 members to raise barriers against Chinese goods would broaden a policy that has so far been applied mainly bilaterally. For chemical and adhesive technologies producers, the relevant question is less the immediate tariff arithmetic than whether more jurisdictions begin applying trade defence to the same product categories at once, which could redirect Chinese volumes toward whichever markets stay open. Points that may be worth considering include which markets would absorb displaced volumes, and how the parallel push on Iran compliance interacts with existing counterparty screening. The proposal is an argument being made to the G20, not an agreed position.

MarketScreener | Japan Today | Hürriyet Daily News

item.title: Statistics Canada reported annualised growth of 3.3% in the second quarter, the fastest since 2023, led by a 3.6% rise in exports and the first rise in business investment after five quarters of decline; the quarter ended before the 22 August tariffs.
item.description:
The figure beat the first quarter substantially and came with an upward revision: Statistics Canada now puts first-quarter growth at 0.3%, having previously reported an annualised contraction of 0.1%. Exports rose 3.6%, largely on higher auto shipments, and business capital investment rose 2.3%, ending five consecutive quarterly declines; residential investment also contributed. The timing matters for how the number should be read, because the second quarter covers April to June and the current escalation came later: the US imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods on 22 August (sources put the value at USD 20 billion and USD 27.6 billion), and Canada's own tariffs of between 15% and 50% take effect on 8 September. Canada's Secretary of State for Labour, John Zerucelli, announced measures to support businesses and workers most affected, and General Motors reached a tentative agreement with Unifor that would invest CAD 1.1 billion in Canadian plants, including adding the next-generation heavy-duty GMC Sierra at Oshawa.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The headline is stronger than the outlook it describes, because the quarter predates the tariff escalation and the export strength that drove it came from autos, a heavily exposed sector. For suppliers into Canadian automotive, construction and industrial production, the more informative signals may be the return of business capital investment after five negative quarters and the GM commitment, both of which suggest some willingness to keep investing through the dispute. Points that may be worth considering include treating the third-quarter data as the first real test of tariff effects, and watching whether announced plant investment translates into committed spending.

Financial Post | CBC | Associated Press | USA Today | MarketScreener

item.title: The Adhesive and Sealant Council's second-quarter survey found manufacturers, raw-material suppliers and distributors naming rising costs and pricing pressure as their top business challenge, with tariffs and the Middle East conflict cited as drivers.
item.description:
The council's quarterly survey of the adhesive and sealant chain reported that pricing pressure and rising costs were the leading business challenges in the second quarter, with uncertainty from tariffs and the Middle East conflict pushing up raw-material and energy costs. Volatility continued through the quarter, affecting supply chains, price management and cost control. Sentiment was not uniformly negative: positive assessments of the current state of the industry rose to 56% from 44% in the previous survey. A separate finding points the same way on priorities. The 2026 Thomson Reuters Global Trade Report found that supply-chain management is now the dominant strategic priority for 68% of trade professionals surveyed across North America, the EU and UK, Latin America and Asia-Pacific — close to double the 35% who named it a year earlier — with tariff volatility reshaping sourcing, procurement, technology investment and long-term planning across the chemical industry.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

These two surveys describe the industry's own reported experience rather than an external read of it, which makes them a useful benchmark. Cost and pricing pressure being named ahead of demand suggests the binding constraint through the second quarter was margin rather than volume, and the near-doubling of trade professionals placing supply chain at the top of their agenda indicates that sourcing decisions are being reweighted toward resilience. Points that may be worth considering include how internal cost and price-recovery experience compares with the 56% positive sentiment reported across the sector, and whether procurement priorities have shifted by a similar degree.

Adhesives & Sealants Industry | Adhesives & Sealants Industry

item.title: Nepal's finance minister put rebuilding after the Himalayan flood at USD 4–5 billion, the electricity authority reported 431 megawatts offline — over 12% of national capacity — and search operations were suspended in bad weather.
item.description:
Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle put the reconstruction bill at USD 4–5 billion, and Nepal has asked for foreign technical assistance. The Nepal Electricity Authority said 431 megawatts of generating capacity had gone dark, more than 12% of the country's total, after floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli valleys damaged or destroyed 14 hydroelectric projects, six of them still under construction; a solar plant on the Trishuli at Nuwakot was largely buried. At the Trishuli-1 project, 63 Indian workers were rescued from a construction tunnel and more than 100 remain unaccounted for. Reported death tolls have continued to rise, reaching 675 in later accounts, and reported missing totals differ, from more than 2,400 in one account to nearly 3,000 in another, including at least 540 foreigners, many of them Indian pilgrims. Rescue work halted on both sides for different reasons. Nepal suspended search and rescue because of bad weather. On the Chinese side, teams were ordered back a kilometre after a lake dammed by debris began to overflow its banks, with state media reporting it could reach about three million cubic metres. India has offered to supply any additional power Nepal needs and has sent relief supplies, and a 16-kilometre queue of freight vehicles formed at the Sonauli border crossing.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The direct commercial exposure for most manufacturers is small, but three effects reach further. A reconstruction programme of USD 4–5 billion in a country of Nepal's size implies a multi-year demand pulse for construction materials, if it is funded. The loss of more than a tenth of generating capacity has prompted India to offer whatever additional power Nepal needs. And the disruption to India–Nepal freight, alongside the mudslide damage at Gyirong Port on the Chinese side, affects routes on both sides at once. Points that may be worth considering include the concentration of hydropower assets in glacial-flood corridors, which this event has exposed.

MarketScreener | Business Standard | China Daily | The Boston Globe | The Economic Times | Tagesschau | Business Standard

item.title: China's housing, land and financial regulators required pre-sold homes to reach main-structure topping-out before sale, with mortgage funds released after completion, and told local authorities to prioritise finished-home sales on newly granted land.
item.description:
The circular was issued on 28 August by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Ministry of Natural Resources and the National Financial Regulatory Administration, with the central bank also named in some reporting. It directs local authorities to promote the direct sale of finished homes so that buyers get "what you see is what you get", to reduce delivery disputes and to prevent delivery risk. Pre-sale is restricted rather than abolished: pre-sold homes must reach the "main structure topped out" stage before they can be sold, and bank mortgage funds are disbursed only after a project is completed and filed for record. Finished-home sales are to be prioritised for projects on newly granted land and on transferred land without a construction planning permit, and encouraged for projects that already hold permits. Existing rules on pre-sale conditions and the supervision of pre-sale funds continue to apply to projects permitted before the circular. Separately, the financial regulator issued measures raising the borrower debt-to-income limit for individual housing loans to 60% from 55% and extending the maximum loan term to 40 years from 30.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Construction is among the largest end-markets for adhesive technologies, so a change in how Chinese housebuilding is financed could affect the shape and timing of demand rather than only its level. Requiring structures to be topped out before pre-sale moves developer cash inflows later in the build cycle, which may favour better-capitalised developers and could slow project starts during the transition, while the emphasis on finished-home sales and delivery quality points toward more work on fit-out, sealing and finishing at the point of completion. The looser mortgage terms pull the other way, toward supporting demand. Points that may be worth considering include how a shift in developer financing might change order timing for construction chemicals in China.

China Daily | China Economic Net | Commercial Times | Cnyes | China Economic Net

item.title: President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran's exports and imports have fallen 25% to 35% in recent months under the US naval blockade, an acknowledgement he had resisted, having previously insisted the sanctions would achieve nothing.
item.description:
Pezeshkian said the country is in a war situation and must accept wartime conditions, and argued that petrol prices should rise to reflect the fall in trade; Vice-President Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah said the blockade has prevented Iran from importing enough petrol to cover a domestic production shortfall. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged action on inflation and unemployment. Pezeshkian noted that Iran sold around 90 million barrels of oil during the short-lived memorandum of understanding signed with Washington in June, when sales were briefly permitted. Diplomatic activity is now centred on the Strait of Hormuz: Qatar is pressing Iran to restore freedom of navigation, and Iran has agreed to prepare conditions for restoring normal shipping, though talks between Tehran and Washington remain stalled. On 30 August Trump wrote that Iran's Kharg Island energy hub was being "blown to smithereens", in a one-line post accompanied by an AI-generated video clip; no other evidence of an attack on the facility emerged.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

An admission of economic damage from Iran's own president, combined with Qatari mediation on Hormuz, is a signal that the shipping disruption behind elevated energy and feedstock costs might eventually ease. That would matter to chemical and adhesive technologies producers through freight rates, naphtha and energy prices, and Gulf routing. The signal is early and reversible: talks are stalled, and Kharg handled about 90% of Iran's pre-war oil exports, so any real move against it would push in the opposite direction. Points that may be worth considering include how much of current cost planning assumes the disruption persists through the winter.

Al Jazeera | Asharq Al-Awsat | The Economic Times | Daily Times | MarketScreener

item.title: Kevin Warsh told the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole symposium the central bank would "have work to do" if it is not confident inflation is returning to 2%, and market-implied odds of a September increase rose from 35.4% to 55.7%.
item.description:
In his debut speech at the symposium, the Federal Reserve chair said the Fed must be confident that underlying inflation is moving toward its objective clearly and at sufficient speed. Commentators read the remarks as a deliberate, limited piece of guidance from a chair who has argued that a quieter and more purposeful Fed communicates better; he also returned to the importance of the money supply. According to CME Group's FedWatch tool, the probability attached to an increase at the September meeting moved from 35.4% on Thursday to 55.7% after the speech, and equities and two-year yields both rose. The inflation data give the argument something to work with: figures cited by market analysts put the July headline personal consumption expenditures price index at 3.7% year-on-year and the core measure at 3.3%, both above the 2% target. Separately, the Financial Times reported that US factory activity reached its strongest level in over four years in July after six months of expansion, with around 30,000 manufacturing jobs added this year.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

A higher US policy rate raises the cost of capital for the construction and industrial projects that draw on adhesive technologies, and for producers' own investment programmes. A move by the Federal Reserve would also come at a time when some European Central Bank Governing Council members favour an increase of their own, which may limit how far transatlantic currency effects diverge. Points that may be worth considering include how sensitive the North American demand outlook is to another increase in financing costs, and whether the reported strength in US factory activity is showing up in order patterns. The probability is above half rather than settled, so the September decision remains genuinely open.

Channel News Asia | MarketScreener | Handelsblatt | Financial Times | Commercial Times | Dünya Gazetesi

item.title: Ifo's business-situation indicator for the German chemical industry rose to plus 11.6 points in August from minus 14.6 in July, its first positive reading since July 2022, which Ifo attributes to Asian supply failures caused by the Hormuz blockade.
item.description:
The improvement was broad across the Ifo survey. The headline business-climate index for the sector, which combines current conditions with expectations, climbed to minus 2.4 points from a seasonally adjusted minus 26.3 in July, and the export-business barometer rose to plus 10.1 from minus 22.7. Supply conditions eased at the same time: 13.8% of chemical companies reported material shortages in the third quarter, down from around a third previously. The Ifo institute's explanation is specific rather than general. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted deliveries of natural gas and other chemical raw materials to Asia, and chemical producers there are suffering more than their European counterparts, which has shifted demand toward German suppliers. Ifo researcher Anna Wolf described the effect as a "special boom". The institute cautioned that the rebound remains heavily dependent on those global supply disruptions, and that underlying conditions are still weak: German chemical production remains about 20% below 2021 levels, and the structural problems facing the sector are not resolved.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

This is the most directly relevant reading of the week for adhesive technologies producers, because it describes the conditions in their own upstream market rather than an adjacent one. Order books and export demand appear to have improved for German chemical production, and easing material shortages could reduce the input-availability pressure of recent quarters. The qualification Ifo attaches is the part that may matter most for planning: the gain is tied to a competitor region being disrupted, so it could reverse if Asian supply normalises or if the Hormuz position changes. Points that may be worth considering include whether current order strength is being read as structural recovery in internal forecasts, and how quickly volumes could unwind if Asian producers return.

MarketScreener | Handelsblatt | Die Zeit | Frankfurter Rundschau | Handelsblatt
